paper_title: New Exclusion Limits for the Search of Scalar and Pseudoscalar Axion-Like Particles from "Light Shining Through a Wall"
suggested_experiment_name: OSQAR (Optical Search for QED vacuum birefringence, Axions and photon Regeneration)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper reports two separate exclusion limits from the 2014 OSQAR LSW campaign: pseudoscalar ALPs constrained to g_agamma < 3.5×10^-8 GeV^-1 and scalar ALPs to g_agamma < 3.2×10^-8 GeV^-1, both valid in the nearly massless limit (m_A < 2×10^-4 eV). The primary result quoted in the abstract and conclusion is the pseudoscalar limit of 3.5×10^-8 GeV^-1. Both limits are encoded as mass-independent (flat) bounds spanning the stated validity range [0, 2×10^-4 eV]. The experiment uses the Light Shining Through a Wall (LSW) method with a 9 T transverse magnetic field over 2×14.3 m, 18.5 W laser at 532 nm, and a CCD detector. No regenerated photons were detected. The Bayesian analysis yielded posterior probability distributions with 95% C.L. upper limits on the reconverted photon rate, from which coupling limits were derived via Eqs. 3 & 4. The paper reports limits of g_Aγγ < 3.5 × 10^-8 GeV^-1 and g_Aγγ < 3.2 × 10^-8 GeV^-1 for pseudoscalar and scalar searches respectively in the nearly massless limit (m_A < 2 × 10^-4 eV).
